key_insight: V-DUGKS reformulates compressible-flow kinetic modeling with coupled vectorial distributions and second-order Hermite equilibrium so it can recover Navier-Stokes physics more efficiently and with adjustable Prandtl number.
engineering_relevance: The scheme offers a more stable and efficient finite-volume solver for continuum compressible flows, making it attractive for shock, vortex, and other high-speed CFD applications.
method: Uses coupled mass, momentum, and energy distribution functions with separate relaxation for momentum and energy transport.
Truncates equilibrium distributions at second-order Hermite level and evaluates moments with fourth-order Gauss-Hermite quadrature.
Employs finite-volume characteristic fluxes plus trapezoidal collision integration, with compact discrete velocity sets.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful tests on shock-tube, Shu-Osher, 2D Riemann, and 3D Taylor-Green vortex cases, with about 2.2-2.9× speed-up in the 3D Taylor-Green vortex case.
watch_item: Performance and stability gains may depend on careful choice of reference temperature, discrete velocity set, and relaxation parameters when implementing the compact vectorial formulation.
paper_title: Vectorial discrete unified gas kinetic scheme for continuum compressible flows
